text: 你设法安抚了惊慌的向导。“教授，你说得对，”她说，“族里会把这些故事讲给孩子们听。但我……和你一样理性。”过了一会儿，她凑近些，压低声音。“那些脚印和我小时候见过的一些很像。就在前一晚，我们村里有个孩子失踪了。”她眼中又浮现出恐惧。“人们说，被小灵——普克-乌吉——抓走的人再也回不来。或者更糟，他们确实回来了，但已经不是原来的那个人。”
尽管你仍抱有怀疑，还是耐心听查理讲述。谈过之后，向导平静了许多，能够继续前进。

en.title: Alone Against the Frost · 35
text: You manage to calm down the distraught guide. “You speak the truth, Professor,” she says. “My people tell these stories to our children. But I am… rational, like you.” After a few moments, she draws closer and lowers her voice. “The tracks are like some I saw when I was a girl. The night before, a child of our village had vanished.” A hint of fear returns to her eyes. “They say that when someone is taken by the Little Ones—the puk-woogies—they do not come back. Or worse, they do come back. But they are not the same.”
Although skeptical, you listen to Charlie’s stories with patience. Talking it out has helped your guide, and she is fit to go on.
